title.en: Know the format of the journal
Pass simple and compound journal entries

say.en: Just as a diary records events day by day, the journal records every transaction in the order of date, showing which account is debited and which is credited. In this lesson: Know the format of the journal.
Pass simple and compound journal entries.

body.en: The *journal* is the book of original (prime) entry. It has five columns: Date, Particulars, Ledger Folio (L.F.), Debit amount and Credit amount. In the particulars column the account to be debited is written first with "Dr", the account to be credited on the next line beginning with "To", and below it a short narration explaining the transaction. Recording in the journal is called journalising.
body.kn: ರೋಜು ಪುಸ್ತಕ ಮೂಲ ನಮೂದು ಪುಸ್ತಕ. ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ದಿನಾಂಕ, ವಿವರ, ಖಾತೆ ಪುಟ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ, ಡೆಬಿಟ್ ಮೊತ್ತ ಮತ್ತು ಕ್ರೆಡಿಟ್ ಮೊತ್ತ ಎಂಬ ಐದು ಕಾಲಂಗಳಿವೆ. ಕೆಳಗೆ ಸಂಕ್ಷಿಪ್ತ ವಿವರಣೆ ಬರೆಯಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.

prompt.en: Put the steps of journalising a transaction in the right order.

steps.en: Identify the accounts the transaction affects
Classify each account: asset, liability, capital, revenue or expense
Decide whether each account increases or decreases
Apply the rules to decide which account is debited and which credited
Write the date in the date column
Write the account debited, followed by Dr, with its amount in the debit column
On the next line write To and the account credited, with its amount in the credit column
Write a short narration below the entry

explanation.en: First analyse (accounts, their class, increase or decrease, debit or credit), then write: date, debit line, credit line beginning with To, and the narration.

body.en: A simple entry has one debit and one credit. A *compound* entry has more than one debit or credit, for example when a machine is bought partly for cash and partly on credit. Goods bought for resale are debited to Purchases, but assets bought for use, such as furniture or machinery, are debited to their own accounts.
